Fact checks›Police & fire

The claim

The money pays for a city police department

“The increase pays for the city's own police department.”

Seen: Recurring in comment threads whenever the Sheriff's contract comes up.

Our finding Not accurate

The record contradicts it.

Eagle Mountain employs no police officers and no firefighters. Patrol is bought from the Utah County Sheriff's Office; fire and ambulance come from Unified Fire Authority, which bills residents on a separate line of the same tax notice.

The numbers

City police officerspatrol contracted from the county Sheriff0
City firefightersUnified Fire Authority, on its own levy0
City "public safety" staffcrossing guards4.82 FTE

What’s true

The money does pay for policing. The affected budget on the impact schedule is the Sheriff's contract, and the deputies it funds are assigned to the Eagle Mountain division.

Where it goes wrong

It is a contract, not a department. The city's audited schedule shows 4.82 full-time equivalents under public safety and every one of them is a crossing guard; the line for firefighters and officers reads zero, and has read zero in all eleven years that schedule covers. Fire and ambulance are not the city's at all: Unified Fire Service Area levies 0.001650 directly, which is nearly twice the city's own new rate.

More detail

This matters for reading a tax bill. Someone comparing Eagle Mountain's rate against a neighboring city that runs its own police and fire is comparing a city that buys those services against one that levies for them, and the neighbor's higher rate is partly that difference.

Where this comes from

Every finding here is drawn from an open-meeting recording or a published document. Check it yourself.
